applicable_failures: The scan only handled .docx, .xlsx, .eml, .txt and .md files; every other file type hit `*) exit 0` and was skipped (e.g. PDFs). The agent still reports 'all 9,288 files' scanned, and no file-type census was run to show nothing was missed.

The regex needs 'cascade' within 80 characters of 'retail' or 'holdings', or a standalone 'CRH'. Bare 'Cascade' mentions, 'Cascade Retail' split across XML tags, and variants like 'Cascade Ret.' would be missed. The docx text is stripped only by splitting on '<', so a name split across runs breaks the match.

Coverage of every matter was never confirmed: no per-matter file counts or scanned-file counts exist. The prior runs were killed or timed out, and the final run's output was only polled, so there is no completeness check.
critique.concerns: The scan finished with 20 hits across seven matters, but the claim of full coverage is unsupported. Unhandled file types were silently skipped and the pattern is narrow. Nearly all hits are emails, so matters whose Cascade references appear only in agreements or PDFs could be missing. Hit matters also include a term-sheet email (1012-00001), which may be out of scope.
critique.recommendation: Count files by extension across documents/matters and extract any unscanned types such as PDFs. Rerun with a looser case-insensitive 'cascade' pattern, collecting matter IDs without output caps. Also run a path and folder search by client name. Then open every hit matter's key documents, not just the email hits.
